newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Close race in view for 1996 Sakharov prize.
newsitem.headline: Close race in view for 1996 Sakharov prize.

text.p: Political group leaders in the European Parliament have two weeks to decide if they should award the 1996 Sakharov prize for freedom of thought to a Cuban lawyer, a Mexican bishop or a Chinese dissident.

The main race for the 15,000-Ecu prize is between Leonel Morejon Almagro, a leading member of the pro-democracy coalition known as the Concilio Cubano, and Don Samuel Ruiz, president of the Mexican Episcopal Commission for Indigenous Peoples.
Both were selected by 23 votes by the parliament's foreign affairs committee on Thursday.
A third candidate, leading Chinese political prisoner Wei Jingsheng, was selected by four votes.
On October 17 the leaders of the parliament's eight political groups must decide which of the three will receive the prize at a ceremony in Strasbourg in December.
Morejon, officially backed by the right-wing European People's Party (EPP) and the Union for Europe, is expected to win the support of the Europe of Nations and Liberal groups.
The Concilio Cubana is made up of 140 non-official groups that include a number of well-known Cuban dissidents.

Awarding the Sakharov prize to Morejon, though controversial, would be one way of showing Washington that there are more constructive ways of promoting democratic reform in Cuba than by tightening the U.S. embargo against Havana, an EPP official told Reuters.
The General Affairs Council said on Tuesday it would challenge at the World Trade Organisation a U.S. law under which EU companies could be penalised for trading with Cuba.
Ruiz, the candidate of the left-wing Socialist and United Left groups, is also expected to win the support of the Green group.
The bishop has been nominated three times for the Nobel Peace Prize for his role as mediator in the 1994 conflict between the Mexican government and indigenous rebels in Chiapas.

The decision of the small, left-wing Radical Alliance could be decisive in determining who wins the prize, which last year went to the Kurdish parliamentarian Leyla Zana, who has been imprisoned by the Turkish authorities.

Wei, the Radicals' original candidate, appears to be out of the running and the group is deeply divided over which of the other two nominees to back, according to one of the group's foreign affairs officials.
Some are inclined to side with the other left-wing groups behind Bishop Ruiz.

But the French Radical deputies are reluctant to back a religious figure, the official told Reuters, and could well persuade the group to back Morejon, who has been declared a prisoner of conscience by Amnesty International.
